messages:
Maria Chen: Quick heads-up — seeing noisy deltas when comparing canary -> baseline for traffic split 10/90 in the last 6h. p99 latency jumps look correlated with short request bursts, makes the canary signal unstable.
Akshay Patel: Are we sure it's not just sampling? those 10% sessions might be tiny sample sizes for some slices.
Jess O'Neil: Yep, sample size is my first thought. We should add a minimum-samples guard before raising alerts. Right now the guard only looks at relative delta and absolute threshold.
Samira Khan: Agree. Proposed rules:
- require min 500 requests per minute per slice
- compute delta over 5m rolling window and 30m baseline
- ignore slices with high variance (coefficient of variation > 0.5)
Akshay Patel: Also we could switch to a weighted z-score instead of raw percent delta so small baseline values don't blow up.
Maria Chen: Good call. For visibility in the console, I want an annotated heatmap of slice stability (p50/p95/p99 variance) with a toggle to overlay deployments/infra incidents.
Jess O'Neil: UI-wise, we can add a "stability" column in rollout details: green/yellow/red and a compact tooltip with recent spike times and links to traces.
Samira Khan: For alerts, propose two tiers: "soft" (notify channel, do not autofallback) and "hard" (trigger fallback policy). Soft fires on borderline z-score and low volume; hard requires z-score>3 AND min-samples AND sustained for 3 consecutive windows.
Maria Chen: That avoids noisy rollbacks. Can we test this in staging with a synthetic burst generator?
Akshay Patel: Yes, I can run a 5-10m burst at 50 req/s into the canary and baseline slices and record. Also will add a jittered traffic pattern to mimic real-world.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout 2026-03-15T09:12:03Z started for service/text-gen@v2.1 :rocket:
Jess O'Neil: For metric computation I'm sketching a PromQL-ish query we can adapt in the telemetry pipeline:

```
# per-slice p99 over 5m
slice_p99 = histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, slice))
# baseline rolling avg
baseline_p99 = avg_over_time(slice_p99[30m])
delta_z = (slice_p99 - baseline_p99) / stddev_over_time(slice_p99[30m])
```

We then apply min_samples = sum(rate(request_count[5m])) by (slice) > 500.
Akshay Patel: That looks good, just make sure to use stable labels (no instance id) and to backfill NaNs as high variance so they don't trigger.
Samira Khan: Can we also expose the raw sample counts in the drilldown so SREs can quickly see if an alert was due to low sample size?
Maria Chen: Yes — drilldown should show a small histogram of recent request counts and a sparkline of the delta_z so it's obvious when data is flaky.
Jess O'Neil: UX question: where do we place the "soft" vs "hard" settings? Per-rollout defaults + per-customer override? I think default at rollout-level, with override on dedicated deployments.
Akshay Patel: Agreed. Defaults sensible for hosted: soft threshold = 2, hard = 3, min_samples = 500. Allow customers to tighten.
Samira Khan: I'll draft the guard config schema:
```
{
 "min_samples": 500,
 "window_mins": 5,
 "baseline_window_mins": 30,
 "soft_z": 2,
 "hard_z": 3,
 "min_sustain_windows": 3,
 "ignore_high_variance": 0.5
}
```
Maria Chen: Perfect. Last item: telemetry retention for these slices — need at least 2h raw to support rolling windows + 30m baseline; prefer 24h for postmortems. Ops, is that OK cost-wise?
Akshay Patel: 24h fine for most services. For very high-throughput ones we can downsample after 2h.
Jess O'Neil: I'll mock a dashboard: top-left heatmap of slices by stability, right panel drilldown with sample counts + delta sparkline, bottom timeline with deployment annotations. Will share a screenshot tomorrow.
Maria Chen: Thanks. Action items:
- Akshay: run synthetic burst and send results (ETA today EOD)
- Jess: dashboard mock + PromQL variants (ETA tomorrow)
- Samira: draft guard schema + make_min_samples required in rollout API (ETA today)
- Maria: follow up with product on per-customer overrides (ETA tomorrow)
( :thumbsup: )
